What to look for: this shader compiles with exit 0 on both panes (dxc 1.6.2112, the release
that introduced -HV 2021 support, and dxc_trunk) and neither pane prints a
`-Wfor-redefinition` / "shadows declaration in the outer scope" warning about the inner
`for (uint i = ...)` shadowing the outer `uint i = 7`. Compile the same source with `-HV 2018`
instead (see variant-hv2018-control-main-debug.txt) and that warning appears. The absence is
not a regression in the warning logic: with `-HV 2021` genuine block scoping applies (grep
`ParseStmt.cpp` for `HLSLVersion < hlsl::LangStd::v2021`), so the loop's `i` is a distinct
variable in its own scope rather than a same-scope redefinition of the outer `i`, and the
merge-conflict code path that emits this warning is only reached pre-2021 for the legacy
"for-loop variable leaks into the enclosing scope" behaviour it exists to soften. DXC has no
general shadow warning for ordinary block-scope shadowing in either language mode (see
variant-block-shadow-hv2021-main-debug.txt and variant-block-shadow-hv2018-main-debug.txt).
